Common Addiction Medicine Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

MAT drug billed with wrong NDC code, triggering payer edit failure and claim rejection.

PMEX confirms the correct NDC for every MAT drug dispensed and submits with the correct J-code and NDC on every claim.

Residential SUD treatment denied because ASAM level of care criteria not documented.

PMEX confirms ASAM level of care documentation is on file before billing residential or PHP SUD claims.

IOP billed at the wrong H-code for the level of service intensity documented.

PMEX applies the correct H-code for the specific SUD service intensity per the documented level of care.

Payer applying stricter SUD benefit rules than mental health benefits in violation of MHPAEA.

PMEX identifies MHPAEA parity violations and supports the practice in filing parity complaints with documented comparisons.

Prior authorization not obtained before residential SUD admission.

PMEX manages SUD prior authorization before the admission date is confirmed for all residential and PHP levels of care.

Drug testing claims not coordinated with SUD treatment dates, generating bundling flags.

PMEX coordinates toxicology billing with SUD treatment dates to confirm correct billing on each date of service.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Addiction Medicine Billing

Addiction medicine practices lose 22 to 38 percent of revenue to authorization failures, ASAM documentation gaps, and MAT drug billing errors.

PATTERN 01

Residential SUD Treatment Denied, ASAM Not Documented

Patient admitted to residential SUD treatment. Prior authorization obtained. Claim submitted. Payer requests ASAM level of care assessment at admission. Assessment was conducted but not submitted with the claim. $6,400 residential claim denied pending documentation.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms ASAM level of care documentation is compiled and on file before the first residential claim is submitted. Payer requests for supporting documentation are responded to within the payer response window.

PATTERN 02

MAT Drug Billed Without NDC Code

Buprenorphine/naloxone dispensed in office. J-code submitted without the required National Drug Code identifying the specific product dispensed. Claim rejected at clearinghouse. Revenue delayed while NDC is added to the claim.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX submits MAT drug claims with the correct J-code and NDC on every claim, confirming the NDC matches the specific product and strength dispensed per the dispensing record.

PATTERN 03

IOP Denied, Level of Care Not Justified

Intensive outpatient program (IOP) claim submitted. Payer denies: clinical documentation does not support IOP level of care under their coverage criteria. Patient's ASAM score in the chart supports PHP level. IOP was billed without confirming payer criteria were met.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews payer-specific SUD level of care criteria before billing each service level. When the documented ASAM score does not meet the payer criteria for the billed level of care, PMEX flags the claim for clinical review before submission.

Questions

Addiction Medicine Billing Questions Answered

SUD treatment uses a combination of CPT codes and HCPCS H-codes depending on the payer. H-codes (H0001 to H0050) are common for Medicaid and some commercial payers. CPT codes are used by other commercial payers. We apply the correct code set per each payer contract.

MAT drugs such as buprenorphine (J0571 to J0575) and naltrexone (J2315) are billed with the J-code for the drug, the NDC, and the administration or dispensing code. We confirm the correct product, strength, and NDC on every MAT claim.

The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act requires health plans to cover SUD treatment benefits no more restrictively than medical or surgical benefits. When payers apply stricter prior authorization or visit limits to SUD services, this may violate MHPAEA.

ASAM levels (0.5 outpatient to 4.0 medically managed inpatient) correspond to specific billing codes and service intensities. We apply the correct CPT or H-code for the documented ASAM level on every claim.

Yes. We manage prior authorization for residential, partial hospitalization, and intensive outpatient SUD programs, with ASAM level of care documentation and clinical notes submitted with every authorization request.

Within 30 days, with MAT drug billing, SUD authorization tracking, and level of care coding workflows active from day one.
